note: M6 successor layer. It records what M0 could not: step 1 added the public stage boundary, its test and the pre-integration baseline and repaired two stale guards; step 2 records the visible three-scene swap, the three scene components, the re-baselined guards and the two light relation tokens. It never republishes a unit, never widens the Atlas projection and never edits M0.

files.note: Repairs one stale source assertion after the M2 search rewrite moved the landing row onto the shared source adapter. The invariant (the landing is findable at /) is unchanged; the guard no longer demands the old object-literal shape. No app behavior changed. If this pin does not match the recorded M0 addition hash, verification fails.

The negative gate builds its scratch checkout from the receipt manifests. M6 is a successor of M0 and not reachable from it, so the scratch needed one explicit line to copy the M6 manifest and its paths; this edit is that line plus its import.

The byte-identity guard compared content against the raw 28 Oct SQL baseline, so the later audited Atlas extension wave read as damage. The guard now asks the receipt chain whether a successor recorded the exact bytes, which is the invariant the repository already enforces; no content byte changed.

Reshaped into the three-scene client boundary. Selection, the ?insight= restore/pushState contract, scene disclosures, card zones and the dealer pointer tilt are retained; the v3 gate stack, editions rail and scroll-progress choreography are removed. The dealer is mounted inside the timeline scene behind 'Open the edition'.

Builds the stage model once (audience 'review', today = build date) and passes model, items, Atlas and the feed notice to the stage. The Atlas still uses its default fail-closed projection, so the review audience cannot widen it.

Adds the .stage-scene* vocabulary: timeline strip and ticks, peek, actions, dealer disclosure, graph/discovery panel, closing destinations, plus responsive, reduced-motion and forced-colors rules. The retired .stage-gate* rules remain for the gate components the Home no longer mounts.

A review audience with zero withheld edges now falls back to the projection's own notice instead of reporting '0 candidate connections'. The public branch is unchanged, so the /not published yet/ contract still holds.

Light-mode relation marks: --chart-3 #e69f00 -> #c07d00 (2.19:1 -> 3.30:1) and --chart-4 #cc79a7 -> #b85c8f (2.97:1 -> 4.11:1) against #FCFCFC. Same hue families, both above the 3:1 non-text target. Dark tokens unchanged; no other token moved.

Re-baselined for the swap: asserts the three scenes in reading order, the retired gates absent from the Home while their files remain, one dealer behind a disclosure, one buildStageModel call, the timeline's selection-is-not-activation contract, and the archive hand-off in the closing scene. Every pre-existing invariant is kept.
Adds the zero-withheld review fallback guard: with the empty public projection the review model must reuse the projection's notice and contain no 'candidate' vocabulary.

additions.note: Public boundary for the three-scene Home: audience, fifteen-day timeline, graph counts and destinations. Pure module; it never reads storage or the review-preview flag.
Guards for the boundary: audience separation, one edition per day, no borrowed card, no candidate claim or edge object in the public model.
Pre-integration baseline captured before the three-scene Home swap, so the visible change can be compared and reverted byte-for-byte.

Scene 1. Fifteen-day calendar strip from the stage model; a quiet day is a static cell with no control, an edition day is a button. Arrow/Home/End walk editions, Enter opens the disclosed dealer. Roving tabindex, honest empty-day copy, and a narrow-screen scroll that centres the selected edition without moving the page.

Scene 2. The selected edition unfolded with InsightScene and KnowledgeInstrument, then the only graph the audience may see: Atlas peek when state is ready, otherwise the model's notice, counts and site-relative discovery destinations. Draws no candidate edge.

Scene 3. Four real destinations, the review status, the selected edition's lesson/practice/archive hand-offs, the identity strip and the polite live region. No gate, no takeover, no unpublished promise.
